claims.statement: `DJIMITFLO_RUNTIME_PROFILE` (default `api`, invalid values warn and fall back to `api`) is the master arming switch: `operator` adds operator integrations and maintenance loops (Telegram, PromptIntel, retention, cognitive loop closure), `autonomous` adds the loop daemon, meta-orchestration, self-modification, negotiation, capability acquisition, and the event outbox.

`DJIMITFLO_EXPLAINER_AUTONOMY=false` is the opt-out for the explainer fleet worker, which runs in every runtime profile (it still honors the kill-switch); `DASHBOARD_SERVE_ENABLED=false` switches to API-only mode; `DJIMITFLO_BOARD_HANDOFF_AUTONOMY` is default-on inside the autonomous profile.

The server reads `PORT` (default 3001), `HOST` (default 0.0.0.0), `CORS_ORIGINS` (default localhost:5173 pair), `DASHBOARD_PATH`, `BACKUP_DIR`; `DATABASE_DRIVER` selects sqlite (default) vs postgresql with the `PGHOST`/`PGPORT`/`PGDATABASE`/`PGUSER`/`PGPASSWORD`/`PGSSL`/`PG_POOL_SIZE`/`PGSCHEMA` family; `RANSOMWARE_MODULE_ENABLED` defaults on and `RANSOMWARE_MODULE_MODE` defaults to `detect`.

`DJIMITFLO_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` is required in production (explore routes throw without it and it must be http/https, defaulting to `http://localhost:$PORT`), and `/metrics` is default-off — it returns 404 until `METRICS_TOKEN` is set, after which scrapers authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <METRICS_TOKEN>` rather than JWT.

`JWT_SECRET` is required for production startup (AuthService calls `process.exit(1)` when absent in production; dev falls back to a random per-process secret with a warning), `JWT_EXPIRES_IN` defaults to `15m`, and `AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL`+`AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` create the bootstrap admin only when both are set and no users exist (role `admin` by default via `AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_ROLE`).

Spawned runtime CLI children never receive the server's environment by blanket copy: `executor-env.ts` forwards only an allowlist (PATH/HOME, *_BIN_PATH, DJIMITFLO_*_MODEL, DJIMITFLO_CONTROL_URL/SPAWN_TOKEN, provider API keys) plus whatever `RUNTIME_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` names.

`RUNTIME_ALLOW_SKIP_PERMISSIONS` (default false) is the master gate: a per-task `skip_permissions` request is honored only when this env is the literal string `true`; `OPENCODE_SKIP_PERMISSIONS`/`CODEX_SKIP_PERMISSIONS` (both default false) bypass the respective CLI's own permission model and emit a security-override audit event.

`DOCKER_SANDBOX_IMAGE` defaults to `djimitflo-runner:latest` and sandboxed startup throws unless the image is digest-pinned (`@sha256:`); `DOCKER_SANDBOX_SKIP_DIGEST_CHECK=true` bypasses that check with a warning. Sandbox invariants are code-fixed: non-root `DOCKER_SANDBOX_USER` (default 1000:1000), `--cap-drop ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, read-only root with tmpfs /tmp, `--rm` cleanup, `DOCKER_CPU_LIMIT`=1.0, `DOCKER_MEMORY_LIMIT`=512m, `DOCKER_NETWORK_MODE`=none, `DOCKER_TIMEOUT_MS`=600000.
`DJIMIT_DEEP_ENABLED=true` is the opt-in arming flag for the Deep Agents executor and its contract issuer in `ExecutionEngine`; the other eight executors register by default.

The `LoopDaemon` runs only in the autonomous profile; each tick it loads pending goals, sorts by `(risk_class desc, created_at asc)`, and starts as many as fit in available slots, with `GOAL_QUEUE_POLL_MS` (default 5000) and `GOAL_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default 4) as its pacing controls. `LOOP_REVIEWER_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 300000 (clamped [1000,900000]) and `LOOP_DAEMON_CHECK_SCRIPTS`/`LOOP_DAEMON_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 120000, minimum 1000, maximum 600000) scope the daemon's deterministic checks.

`SELF_IMPROVEMENT_OBJECTIVE_LOOP_ENABLED` (default off) is the first path letting a free-text goal drive a real objective-mode maker/checker cycle instead of the safe doc-drift no-op; it requires a self-improvement-source, risk_class `low` goal, and is capped per tick by `SELF_IMPROVEMENT_OBJECTIVE_LOOP_MAX_PER_TICK` (default 1, hard ceiling 3).

`AUTHORITY_GATE` (default `off`) gates every LoopDaemon goal start: `on` observes/emits a DENY authority event, `enforce` fail-closes so a goal without an ALLOW approval record in `authority_events` is refused.

Loop-path budget exhaustion surfaces as first-class HTTP 409 error codes: `LOOP_WORKER_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `LOOP_TOKEN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `LOOP_WALL_CLOCK_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, and `LOOP_RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`.

`GOVERNANCE_GATE_ENABLED` (default off) arms a gate in the task-execution path that only tightens (`allow`→`require_approval`) when the executing agent/model's latest OpenMythos score is below `GOVERNANCE_GATE_FLOOR` (default 3, against a real ~0–95 production range, so operators should set e.g. 30–40); `GOVERNANCE_GATE_MODEL_MAP` maps executor kinds to benchmarked subject models and the evidence lookup order is agent_id → `nightly:<model>` → metadata.subject_model; the gate never loosens a deny, and no evidence means allow.

`DJIMITFLO_FRONTIER_EXPERTS_ENABLED` (default off) gates frontier-expert discovery/council routes (409 FRONTIER_EXPERTS_DISABLED when off); `FRONTIER_EXPERTS_SCHEDULER_ENABLED`+`FRONTIER_EXPERTS_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 60) arm a scheduler that automates discovery/enrichment/peer-review but deliberately stops before the human-only CHECKED→APPROVED→ACTIVE governance wall.

The in-process schedulers share an arming pattern — `start()` returns false unless the corresponding `*_ENABLED` var is the literal `true`, then sets an unref'd interval plus an immediate catch-up tick — and all are default-off: `OPENMYTHOS_NIGHTLY_ENABLED`/`_MODELS`/`_HOUR` (default hour 3, autonomous profile), `COMPLIANCE_REPORT_SCHEDULER_ENABLED`/`COMPLIANCE_REPORT_TYPE`/`COMPLIANCE_REPORT_INTERVAL_HOURS` (default custom/24), `SELF_HEALING_SCHEDULER_ENABLED`/`SELF_HEALING_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 30).

`SELF_IMPROVEMENT_AUTO_REVIEW_ENABLED`/`_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 15) arm the proposal→specialist-review→autonomous-goal loop; `SELF_IMPROVEMENT_REFINEMENT_ENABLED`/`_MAX_PER_TICK` (default 3, hard ceiling 10) is an independently toggled refinement pass; `SPECIALIST_PANEL_BACKLOG_ENABLED`/`_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 15) projects only general consensus_ready panels (excluding self-improvement and memory-candidate panels); `MEMORY_CANDIDATE_REVIEW_ENABLED`/`_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 15) replaces the unsatisfiable score gate with specialist-panel analysis plus an evolution loop.

`MemorySyncService.onTaskCompleted` fans out via `Promise.allSettled` to UAMS (`UAMS_URL`/`UAMS_API_KEY`), Qdrant (`QDRANT_URL`/`QDRANT_API_KEY`, writes optionally separated via `QDRANT_WRITE_URL`/`QDRANT_WRITE_API_KEY`), and an OKF concept file under `OKF_BASE` — so no single sink failure fails the task; embeddings come from Ollama (`OLLAMA_URL`/`OLLAMA_HOST`, `DJIMITFLO_EMBED_MODEL`/`OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL` default `snowflake-arctic-embed:s`, `EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_MS` default 10000) and only ever degrade the Qdrant leg.

Qdrant sync is idempotent and never destroys populated data at a different embedding dimension: task ids map to stable derived point ids, and only an empty mismatched collection is recreated (a populated dimension mismatch is skipped with a warning).

`OKF_BASE` (default the repository `knowledge/`) is the operator-controlled canonical OKF bundle; the legacy `packages/knowledge` path is rejected as non-canonical, and `OKF_VALIDATOR_PATH` (default `tools/validate_okf.py` beside the bundle, must be absolute) runs read-only with a 10s limit — missing/failed validation blocks capability-sync apply, and structural acceptance is not certification.

Telegram has two config surfaces: the webhook routes read `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`/`TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`/`TELEGRAM_USER_MAP`/`TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL` and validate `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` against the `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` header (503/401 on missing/mismatch); separately, `TELEGRAM_BOTS_CONFIG` (JSON array) arms the multi-bot polling gateway in the operator profile only.

The Telegram polling gateway prevents duplicate pollers via filesystem leases in `DJIMIT_TELEGRAM_LEASE_DIR` (default `<os.tmpdir>/djimit-telegram-leases`) with a 30s heartbeat and 2min TTL; SIGTERM must call `stopAll()` or a restart sees EEXIST and skips polling forever.

NestedSpawnService is default-deny: `SPAWN_DEPTH_BUDGET` defaults to 0 (roots cannot spawn children — any value >0 enables nested spawning), and tree budgets are `SPAWN_TREE_TOKEN_BUDGET` (200000), `SPAWN_TREE_WALL_BUDGET_MS` (600000), `SPAWN_TREE_MAX_CONCURRENT_CHILDREN` (4), with per-child grant ceilings `SPAWN_PER_DEPTH_TOKEN_CAP` (50000) and `SPAWN_PER_DEPTH_WALL_CAP_MS` (120000) so a child gets min(remaining, ceiling); a cycle guard and live_route_allowed capability routing also gate every spawn.

`DJIMITFLO_CONTROL_URL` is auto-derived at startup as `http://<dialHost>:<PORT>/api/swarms/spawns` (`127.0.0.1` when HOST is 0.0.0.0/localhost) so a runtime child can call back; `DJIMITFLO_SPAWN_TOKEN_SECRET` (falling back to `JWT_SECRET`, else `SPAWN_TOKEN_SECRET_REQUIRED` in production, else ephemeral per-process in dev/test) signs scoped HMAC spawn tokens (leaseId|spawnTreeId|expiresAt, 30 min TTL, constant-time validated).

Both `/health` and `/api/health` expose the same build-provenance block — `commit`/`built_commit` from `DJIMITFLO_COMMIT_SHA` and `DJIMITFLO_BUILD_COMMIT` (baked into the Docker image from ARG VCS_REF alongside DJIMITFLO_BUILD_SOURCE/DJIMITFLO_BUILD_TIME), plus `instance_id` from `DJIMITFLO_INSTANCE_ID` — and `commit_matches_build` is true only when both commits exist and are equal, so a deployed artifact is attributable only when running and baked revisions agree.

In the MCP server `DJIMITFLO_DATA_MODE` defaults to `snapshot` and must be set to `live` for mutating tools — `requireLiveMode()` throws `DJIMITFLO_LIVE_DATA_REQUIRED` on a snapshot handle, `DJIMITFLO_DATABASE_ID_REQUIRED` when the DB has no `database_instance_id`, and `DJIMITFLO_DATABASE_ID_MISMATCH:<actual>` when `DJIMITFLO_EXPECTED_INSTANCE_ID` disagrees; the DB id itself is a random UUID minted once into `system_state` by `ensureDatabaseInstanceId`, and `DJIMITFLO_NODE_ID`/`DJIMITFLO_RUNTIME_HOST`/`DJIMITFLO_DB` supply node/host/db-path identity.

`DJIMITFLO_FEDERATION_ENABLED` is default-off/no-op when empty (discovery-only reading of external agent commons); `EVENT_PUBLISH_ENABLED` (default off) arms the outbox publishing of work-item/approval/goal domain events onto the event bus configured by `DJIMIT_EVENT_BUS_URL`/`DJIMIT_EVENT_STREAM` (default `djimit.events`)/`DJIMIT_EVENT_BUS_TOKEN`/`DJIMIT_EVENT_POLL_MS` (default 60000).

`LOOP_MAKER_TIMEOUT_MS` sets the daemon's maker execution timeout with default 300000, accepted values clamped to [1000, 600000] — but the mutation lane bypasses it entirely: `daemonMakerTimeoutMs` returns a fixed 600000 for mutation-gap runs (npm ci + two Stryker runs exceeded the old fixed 300 s in production).

The deterministic-check knobs are resolved by `daemonCheckOptions`: `LOOP_DAEMON_CHECK_SCRIPTS` is a comma-separated script list (empty means the repo default check set) and `LOOP_DAEMON_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 120000, is only honored when >= 1000, and is capped at 600000; the repo-wide `test` script cannot finish in 120 s, so hosts scope the script list down.

`LOOP_DAEMON_REPOSITORY_PATH` points objective-mode loop runs at a real git checkout (the production image's cwd is /app, not a repository, so worktree creation fails without it) and is passed to `startObjectiveLoop` only — doc-drift runs ignore it; it is also the fallback repo root for the test-gap/mutation-gap sources and commons grounding.

A maker runtime is never inferred from a recommendation: without `LOOP_DAEMON_MAKER_RUNTIME` (objective mode only) the maker lease stays `manual` and daemon goals die with MANUAL_MAKER_REQUIRES_HUMAN; when set, the operator's explicit choice also takes precedence over the runtime bandit's selection.

`LOOP_BANDIT_ENABLED`/`LOOP_BANDIT_SPECIES` (default off) arm E12 outcome-driven maker selection: Thompson sampling over each species' verified/failed runs in `skill_outcomes` picks the maker species per loop, and a challenger with fewer than 20 outcomes is capped at `LOOP_BANDIT_MAX_SHARE` (default 0.1) of runs.

`LOOP_EVOLVE_ENABLED`/`LOOP_EVOLVE_SPECIES` (default off, at most 2 extra species) arm E13 multi-maker evolution on eligible goals — test-gap/mutation-gap proposals or goals with metadata.evolve=true: sibling makers of other species run the same objective and deterministic fitness (checks, diff budget, mutation score, tokens) keeps only the winner before the reviewers run.

`LOOP_DAEMON_AUTOMATED_CHECKER_ENABLED` (default off) makes the daemon dispatch the checker automatically using the same runtime as the maker (self-review, not an independent reviewer) under `LOOP_REVIEWER_TIMEOUT_MS`; a LOOP_WORKER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED error blocks the goal for human approval rather than being swallowed. `LOOP_DAEMON_AUTOMATED_SECURITY_CHECKER_ENABLED` is a deliberately separate, higher flag that does the same for the security_checker lease and is inert without the base flag.

`AUTONOMY_SHADOW_ENABLED` (default off) records an `auto_approve_shadow` judgment for every human approval a loop run waits for — decision 'yes' only for test-only, non-high-risk, non-security changes whose class has >= 3 verified outcomes and no regression — and approves nothing; failure of the shadow bookkeeping is caught so it can never affect the loop.

`LOOP_AUTO_APPROVE_TEST_GAP` and `LOOP_AUTO_APPROVE_MUTATION_GAP` (both default off) are the first real auto-approves: `testGapAutoApproveScope` returns the proposal's single new test-file artifact, which the daemon writes onto the maker lease as the enforced `auto_approved_scope` before approving, and the mutation lane additionally requires at least one already-verified human-approved mutation-gap run.

`TEST_GAP_SOURCE_ENABLED` (default off) starts the TestGapSourceService in the autonomous profile (6 h interval): untested-but-imported server services become fully grounded test-only proposals capped by `TEST_GAP_MAX_PER_DAY`/`TEST_GAP_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` (default 2/2) over `TEST_GAP_REPO_PATH` (default `LOOP_DAEMON_REPOSITORY_PATH`), and a file that ever had a test-gap proposal is never proposed again automatically. `MUTATION_GAP_ENABLED`/`MUTATION_GAP_MAX_PER_DAY` (default off/2, one in flight) run the parallel mutation-gap lane for tested non-sensitive services of 30–400 lines.

`scripts/mutation-gain.mjs` (npm script `test:mutation:grounded`) is the mutation lane's deterministic fitness check: with `MUTATE_FILE`/`MUTATE_TEST` set it runs Stryker on the committed and the working-tree test and passes when the mutation score gains >= `MUTATE_MIN_GAIN` points (default 10) or reaches 90; without them it exits 0 immediately, so the script is a safe listing in `LOOP_DAEMON_CHECK_SCRIPTS` for all lanes, and the daemon injects both variables from the goal's grounding via `mutationCheckEnv` — which also activates the fixed-600000 mutation-lane maker timeout and the 400-line diff budget.

Worker stdout/stderr evidence lives under `resolveEvidenceRoot()`: `LOOP_EVIDENCE_ROOT` wins, otherwise the `agent-evidence/agentic-control-loop-fleet` directory beside an absolute `DB_PATH` (the persistent volume in prod), falling back to the repo's `.data` for local dev — prod 2026-09-24 wrote evidence into the image's /app/.data and lost it on every deploy, so the default deliberately follows DB_PATH.

`scripts/auto-deploy.sh` runs on the VPS from a systemd timer and self-deploys main only when all preconditions hold: main differs from the commit in compose.yml, every CI check-run completed green, the commit is at least `AUTO_DEPLOY_SETTLE_MIN` (default 20) minutes old, zero loop workers are running (running worker_leases plus running `loop-worker-%` tasks), and no kill-switch file `$DEPLOY_ROOT/AUTO_DEPLOY_DISABLED` (default `/srv/djimitflo/AUTO_DEPLOY_DISABLED`) exists; the deploy uses `deploy-vps.sh` downloaded from the commit being deployed, and each probe (MAIN_SHA/CURRENT_SHA/CHECKS/COMMIT/LEASES/DEPLOY) can be overridden by an evaluated `AD_<NAME>` env var so the decision logic is testable without a VPS.
